FAST
Nov 7 : Elena Rybakina's withdrawal from the WTA Finals on the eve of the season-ending championships is disappointing, but the world number one needs time to recover from the physical toll of a demanding year, tournament director Garbine Muguruza said.
Defending champion Rybakina pulled out of the tournament on Saturday, saying she was not physically ready to compete, leaving Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk to take her place in the eight-player field at Indian Wells. Tournament organizers later said a viral illness was the official reason for the withdrawal.
Muguruza, the former world number one and two-time Grand Slam champion, said she had spoken with Rybakina and that the Kazakh had been unable to recover in time after struggling with physical problems late in the season.
"We love Elena and we know that she was feeling so-so in Tokyo as well," Muguruza told Reuters. "I spoke to her today and she really couldn't recover on time.

"What we want is for her to feel good, to go rest, to recover. We don't want her to feel like she has to play — only if she's ready to."
Rybakina, who won two Grand Slam titles this year, also withdrew from ⁠the ​Tokyo quarter-finals last month ​because of a neck injury.
'AMAZING FIELD'
Rybakina's absence deprives the event of some star power, but Muguruza said the round-robin format and depth of the field would ensure a high-quality tournament.
"We have the best players," said Muguruza, who triumphed at the WTA Finals in Guadalajara in 2021.
"I know our world number one is not going to be able to play, but we have an amazing field, the very best.
"Every match could be a Grand Slam final. You really need to be ready. You cannot give one inch."
Kostyuk, who is making her WTA Finals debut after a breakthrough season that included the Madrid title and a rise into the top 10, was already in Indian Wells as an alternate and practicing when Rybakina withdrew.
Muguruza said the Ukrainian, known for her signature post-match backflip celebrations, had earned her opportunity.
"Marta is great. She's had a breakthrough year," Muguruza said. "With this year, we have many first-time players in the Finals, and that's very exciting. It's very hard to qualify."
Kostyuk has been outspoken about Russia's invasion of Ukraine and does not shake hands with Russian or Belarusian opponents. Muguruza said the tournament would support players in making their own decisions.
"They're free to do whatever they feel," she said. "We are open and supporting them."
OPPORTUNITY FOR SABALENKA
Rybakina's withdrawal could create an opening for world number two Aryna Sabalenka to make inroads in the rankings.
Sabalenka, who won the Indian Wells title earlier this year, has the chance to reduce the gap with Rybakina at the top of the rankings, Muguruza said, while also highlighting Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva as a player comfortable in the California desert.
"Of course, Aryna might be thinking that this can be a good opportunity," Muguruza said.
The WTA moved the Finals to Indian Wells from Riyadh, with Muguruza saying player safety had been the decisive consideration amid conflict in the region.
"It clearly felt no longer safe to be in a region where there is conflict," she said. "Taking care of the players and looking ahead to what could be safe, comfortable and secure, relocating felt the best decision."
Muguruza said players had responded positively to the switch to Indian Wells, where she competed regularly during her career.
"When we knew that Indian Wells could be the next venue, it was just a joy," she said, adding that ticket sales have been strong. "The whole thing is just perfect."
Source: Reuters

efet_body:
singapore
SFA recalls various Bomberry fruit snack products over potential presence of metal
The four Bomberry products being recalled over the potential presence of metal.
PHOTO:
Singapore Food Agency
PUBLISHED ON
October 29, 2026 7:47 PM
BY
Sean Ler
The Singapore Food Agency (SFA) is recalling four Bomberry fruit snack products sold here over the potential presence of metal.
In a media release on Thursday (Oct 29), SFA noted that the Food Standards Australia New Zealand has issued a notification on the product recall.
The agency said that it has directed the importer Little Farms to recall the implicated products as a precautionary measure, adding that the recall is ongoing.
According to SFA, the implicated Bomberry products are:
Bomberry natural blueberries + Belgian chocolate (dark chocolate), 150g
Bomberry natural blueberries + Belgian chocolate (white and milk chocolate), 150g
Bomberry natural raspberries + Belgian chocolate (white and dark chocolate), 150g
Bomberry natural raspberries + Belgian chocolate (white and milk chocolate), 150g
All four recalled products originate from Australia and have "best before" dates of up to and including Jan 20, 2028.
Those who have consumed the affected products and have concerns about their health should seek medical attention, while those who have purchased the affected products should not consume them.
They may also approach their point of purchase for enquiries.
Under the Sale of Food Act, foods known to be unsafe for consumption should not be sold.
This is the second case of food product recall in Singapore this week.
On Oct 26, SFA recalled Arla Protein Salted Caramel Flavour Pudding (200g) over the potential presence of glass fragments.

US blood pressure drug recall does not affect Singapore: HSA

Published

Summarise
中文
HSA said the US recall of Macleods’ blood pressure drug does not affect Singapore because the affected products are not sold here.
The recall covers Tribenzor tablets from two lots after “failed dissolution specifications” raised concerns the medicine may not work properly.
The US FDA made it a Class II recall, meaning possible “temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences”, but serious harm is unlikely.
AI generated
SINGAPORE – A recent recall which resulted in more than 3,700 bottles of blood pressure medicine taken off the shelves in the United States does not affect consumers here, said the Health Sciences Authority (HSA).
Macleods Pharmaceuticals announced in early October that it is recalling certain batches of olmesartan medoxomil, amlodipine and hydrochlorothiazide tablets, sold under the brand name Tribenzor as a
medication for hypertension, or high blood pressure
.
“The affected products manufactured by Macleods Pharmaceuticals are not marketed in Singapore,” said HSA in response to queries from The Straits Times.
“Hence, the product recall in the US does not affect medicines supplied through authorised local distribution channels here.”
The reason given for the recall was “failed dissolution specifications” – that is, the pills did not dissolve as required and as such may not be effective.
The recall covers 3,528 bottles containing 30 tablets and 216 bottles with 90 tablets – from lot 12251163A and lot 12251163B respectively – which expire on May 31, 2027.
On Oct 26, the US Food and Drug Administration classified the recall as Class II, meaning use of the affected medication could cause “temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences” but is unlikely to cause serious health consequences.
Under a Class II recall, consumers can generally continue taking the medication unless advised otherwise.

efet_title: Protein pudding sold in S'pore potentially contains glass fragments, SFA issues recall - Mothership
efet_body:
News
Protein pudding sold in S'pore potentially contains glass fragments, SFA issues recall
Crunchy.
Nicolas Wong
October 27, 2026, 02:42 PM
Photo from Singapore Food Authority
The Arla Protein Salted Caramel Flavour Pudding (200g) is being recalled in Singapore.
Singapore Food Agency (SFA) noted in an Oct. 27 press release that the Food Standards Australia New Zealand has issued a recall on the product due to the potential presence of glass fragments.
As a precautionary measure, SFA has therefore
directed its importer (Trade-Pro Food Distribution Pte Ltd) to do the same.
The product originates from Denmark and the batch has a Best Before date of Apr. 28, 2027.
Do not eat it
Under the Sale of Food Act, foods known to be unsafe for consumption should not be sold, SFA said.
It added that consumers who have purchased the affected product should not eat it. They can contact their point of purchase if they have any enquiries.
Those who have consumed the pudding and have concerns about their health should seek medical attention.
Small fragments of glass, if swallowed, usually get coated in bodily fluids and digested food, and are able to pass harmlessly via bowel movements in one to three days.
However, small flecks can also cause superficial scratches to the lining of the throat, esophagus, or stomach, leading to mild sore throat or temporary irritation.

SINGAPORE – The Singapore Food Agency (SFA) has recalled various chocolate-covered fruit products under the Bomberry brand over concerns
that they may contain metal.
The affected products are Bomberry Natural Blueberries + Belgian Chocolate (150g) in the flavours Dark Chocolate and White & Milk Chocolate, and Bomberry Natural Raspberries + Belgian Chocolate (150g) in the flavours White & Dark Chocolate and White & Milk Chocolate. All four products originate from Australia.
The recall covers products with “best before” dates up to and including Jan 20, 2028.
SFA has directed the importer, Little Farms, to recall the affected products as a precautionary measure, following an earlier recall by Food Standards Australia New Zealand. The recall is ongoing.
Those who have bought the affected products should not consume them, SFA said. Those who have consumed them and have concerns about their health should seek medical advice.
Consumers may contact their point of purchase for inquiries, the agency added.

Singapore Food Agency recalled Arla Protein Salted Caramel Flavour Pudding after a possible glass fragment risk was found in the Danish product.
The 200g pudding has a best before date of April 28, 2027, and importer Trade-Pro Food Distribution was told to recall it as a precaution.
SFA said the recall is ongoing and warned buyers not to eat it; anyone who has eaten it and feels unwell should seek medical advice.
AI generated
SINGAPORE –
The Singapore Food Agency (SFA) has recalled a pudding product from a Danish brand, due to the potential presence of glass fragments.
The item is Arla Protein Salted Caramel Flavour Pudding (200g), which originated from Denmark, and
has a “best before” date of April 28, 2027, SFA said in a media statement on Oct 26.
SFA has directed the importer, Trade-Pro Food Distribution, to recall the implicated product as a precautionary measure following an earlier recall by the Food Standards Australia New Zealand.
The recall is ongoing.
The pudding is sold at FairPrice and Cold Storage supermarkets, as well as online marketplaces including GrabMart, Lazada, Redmart, Shopee and FoodPanda.
Those who bought the implicated product should not consume it, SFA said, while those who have consumed it and have concerns about their health should seek medical advice.
Ingesting glass fragments may lead to cuts or tears in the digestive tract. Anyone who experiences chest or abdominal pain, blood in stool, abdominal bloating, or a fever after ingesting the implicated product should seek medical attention.
Consumers may contact their point of purchase for enquiries, the agency added.
